videos.script:
Last lesson ended with a promise: work that happens later, and a way to say what to do when it does. {{three}} JavaScript has had three ways to write that, in order: callbacks, then promises, then async and await. Each was invented to fix what hurt about the one before.

{{callbacks}} Callbacks are the original. You hand over a function, and it is called when the work is done. Two steps in a row means a callback inside a callback, and errors have to be checked by hand at every level.

{{promises}} A promise is an object that stands for a result that has not arrived yet. You can pass it around, chain steps onto it, and catch every error in one place.

{{await}} Async and await are promises written to look like ordinary code, one line after another. Most new code is written that way, and today you will see that it is still promises underneath.

{{time}} Then the part that saves real time. Four requests, one after another, take four times as long as four at once. And one mistake to recognise on sight: a promise nobody waited for, whose failure turns up somewhere else entirely.
